children: Shares of Hindalco Industries fell 3 per cent on Monday, November 9, even as the Aditya Birla Group company posted healthy July-September quarter results for the financial year 2026-27 (Q2 FY27). The stock came under selling pressure even as the company reported a 58.8 percent year-on-year (YoY) increase in consolidated net profit, supported by strong contributions from its aluminium and copper businesses and improved performance at subsidiary Novelis.
Hindalco shares opened at Rs 953 on the NSE and fell as much as 3 percent to an intraday low of Rs 919.30. At around 10 am, the stock was trading 1.63 per cent lower at Rs 937.65.
Despite the Monday’s decline, brokerages remained largely positive on the stock, maintaining their bullish ratings. The company released its Q2 FY27 earnings last week on Friday.
Hindalco Q2 results

Hindalco Industries’ consolidated net profit grew 58.8 percent to Rs 7,533 crore for the September quarter of FY2026-27, driven by a strong performance across business segments. Net profit in the year-ago period was Rs 4,741 crore.
The company’s income during the second quarter rose to Rs 92,651 crore over Rs 66,771 crore in the year-ago period.

In a statement, Hindalco said this record performance was underpinned by the strength of Hindalco's integrated business model led by a solid primary upstream business complemented by strong contributions from its downstream business.
EBITDA for the second quarter stood at Rs 13,757 crore, up 42 percent year on year.
The copper business recorded its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA, while Novelis maintained its improved performance, supported by the normalisation of operations at Oswego.

However, the company flagged near-term cost pressures in its India aluminium operations. In a media briefing, Hindalco’s managing director Satish Pai said that production cost for its India aluminium business is expected to remain about 5 percent higher in the third quarter largely due to higher coal costs, but should begin moderating in the fourth quarter as the availability of the dry-fuel improves.

Pai said coal prices in the northern region remained high in October, keeping input costs elevated for the company's smelters in the near term. "Q3 will be 5 per cent above Q2. By Q4, costs should start coming down because coal availability in the northern region should improve once winter sets in and power demand in the northern areas declines," Pai said.
Pai, however, stressed the continued tightness in domestic coal supply. Pai said coal inventories at some of the company's plants are at 50 per cent of normal levels.

In contrast, the company's plants in Odisha had coal inventories at normal levels, he said. The company expects the cost pressure to ease in the fourth quarter as coal availability improves with the onset of winter and a moderation in power demand in northern India.

Together, the non-LME-linked businesses accounted for nearly 50 per cent of the company's earnings, underscoring sustainable growth despite volatility in LME prices and global macroeconomic challenges.
What brokerages said on Hindalco
CLSA on Hindalco share: Outperform, Target Price Rs 1240

CLSA maintained its ‘Outperform’ rating on Hindalco with a target price of Rs 1,240, noting that Novelis' adjusted EBITDA per tonne stood at $553, below its estimates, despite a $39 million benefit from Oswego insurance recoveries, equivalent to around $43 per tonne.
The brokerage said while Oswego production normalised, this has resulted in higher tariff costs $85 per tonne. The South Korea strike had an estimated impact of $20 per tonne.
Although the strike has been resolved, CLSA expects a similar impact by Novelis in Q3 FY27. It added that tariff headwinds should taper to near zero by Q4 FY27 as onshore production increases.

The brokerage said Bay Minette remains on track for commercial shipments from Q1 FY28, with full utilisation expected within two years. CLSA also expects Novelis to return to positive free cash flow (FCF) and begin deleveraging from Q4 FY27, supported by tapering capex and further insurance recoveries.
JPMorgan on Hindalco share: Overweight, Target Price Rs 1165

Global brokerage firm JPMorgan maintained its ‘Overweight’ outlook on Hindalco with a target price of Rs 1,165. The brokerage said Novelis posted an in-line second-quarter with adjusted EBITDA (excluding insurance recovery) growing 11 percent YoY to $469 million.

The brokerage said its net debt-to-EBITDA increased QoQ to 4.7 times (vs. 1Q at 4.5x) but management reiterated that Q4 FY27 will see a decline to 4x and a return to positive free cash flow (capex slowdown, WC release). It further said the Bay Minette commissioning remains on track with first coil produced in September 2026.
JPMorgan also highlighted that Oswego fire insurance recovery is progressing with 1H at $519 million and guidance is for $900 million by end FY27 and a total of $1.3 billion by next year.

Novelis continued to face tariff-related headwinds with 2Q seeing a $78 million impact led by an increase in Canadian shipments from Kingston to meet customer requirements at U.S. Oswego (where supply chain is gradually normalizing). This will ease by end FY27 as Novelis shifts more production to U.S, said the brokerage.
It said Novelis also announced the departure of its CFO (effective mid-Jan 2027) with the company yet to announce a replacement.
Motilal Oswal on Hindalco share: BUY | CMP: Rs 958 | Target Price: Rs 1,180 | Upside 23%
Motilal Oswal reiterated its ‘Buy’ rating on Hindalco with a target price of Rs 1,180, implying an upside potential of around 23 percent from its cited market price of Rs 958.
The brokerage said Hindalco posted strong earnings in Q2 FY27, primarily driven by favourable premiums, better domestic product mix, and higher by-product pricing along with Novelis earnings.

Going forward, it said it believes the earnings outlook for the India operations to stay strong and Novelis started recovering from Oswego-led volume disruption, resulting in additional cost to service customer. “We expect 2H earnings to remain muted for both India operation and Novelis on account of higher cost of production and aluminum price reversal to USD3,100/t from the peak USD3,850/t. However, the strong volume outlook in 2H will support earnings against price moderation,” it added.
Motilal Oswal has also increase FY27 revenue, EBITD and PAT estimates by over 5 percent, factoring in the strong Q2 earnings beat, led by high premiums and by-product realization.
At its cited market price, the stock was trading at 5.7 times FY28 estimated EV/EBITDA and 1.4 times price-to-book value, the brokerage said.
(With PTI inputs)
